label: Inconsistency eliminates a worldview everywhere; a survivor needs an explicit coverage premise
paraphrase: For every interpretation with truth-functional negation: a worldview with no common model (not WORLDVIEW_CONSISTENCY_1) is false at every world. For any family of candidate worldviews, if some candidate is true at the actual world (the explicit coverage premise) and every candidate other than k is inconsistent, candidate k is true at the actual world. Without coverage this fails: in the existing two-world control, an inconsistent rival and the consistent duty-denying worldview leave a survivor that is false at the actual world, and no candidate is true there. A coherent-but-false worldview is not eliminated by consistency tests.
